items.title: Ed Polcer interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: And of course at that time there were still Tommy Dorsey’s “Boogie Woogie,” and Benny Goodman and a few others.

ctx.x: Well I don’t know. I guess I didn’t listen too much to it because I really enjoyed this swing and I think even going, when we got into high school we used to have noontime

dances in high school. It was five days a week. The Student Council would charge two cents admission and with that money that they’d collect every day, once a week we’d go out and buy records. And of course at that time there were still Tommy Dorsey’s “Boogie Woogie,” and Benny Goodman and a few others. So in addition to the pop singers in the early 50s, because I was president of the Student Council, I’d go out and buy some jazz records, and kids were dancing every noontime in the gym. It was incredible. It…
That’s pretty interesting that the high school kids would be doing that much dancing. Nowadays it seems like touching each other —
